🐾 Here’s the story behind Matt’s payments work at **JP Morgan Chase**.

From **August 2009 to June 2012**, Matt served as Technology Delivery Lead for ACCESS Next Generation, the bank’s global corporate banking portal. Its regional payment systems had different data models, connectivity, entitlements, and compliance records. Bottomline Technologies’ WebSeries platform provided the foundation, but the bank needed payment modules and controls well beyond its out-of-box capabilities. Legacy entitlement changes alone took days of manual configuration.

Matt managed a blended team of **40+** **Accenture** and bank resources across Mumbai, Bangalore, and the US. He spent **70 to 80%** of his time embedded at Bottomline’s Portsmouth offices, working out where native platform capabilities ended and bespoke engineering was required, rather than treating ACCESS as a standard WebSeries deployment.

He designed and delivered ACH, wire, FX/cross-border, and federal tax payment modules, including NACHA file validation, foreign exchange engine integration, and Message Authentication Code payment verification. He also built payment-type-specific permissions, so a user could approve wires without being authorized to initiate FX payments. Role-based profiles and bulk permission changes replaced individual configuration, reducing entitlement management from **days to minutes**.

For the global gateway, Matt designed message transformation, protocol translation, and routing across **12 countries**, connecting ACCESS to clearing networks and internal compliance, settlement, and reporting systems. He also led payments data migration, introducing compliance dashboards, preserving regulatory traceability, and running production validation and post-cutover defect triage.

ACCESS launched in **April 2011**, serving **135,000+** corporate, financial institution, government, and municipal clients across **180+ countries**. The gateway gave corporate treasurers a single entry point for regional payments, and the legacy migration completed **without disruption to live payment operations**.

🐾 Here’s how Matt describes his leadership philosophy.

Matt leads with empathy, clarity, and purpose. He describes himself as having a “builder’s mindset, coach’s heart” and teaches teams to fish rather than just fixing problems.

Many engineering teams he inherited were “over-processed, under-trusted, waiting for permission instead of owning outcomes.” His response was to make intent explicit, push decisions to the people closest to the work, and coach teams to think clearly rather than simply execute tasks. He uses transparency, direct feedback, and open communication so people can raise problems and challenge assumptions.

At **Accenture’s** Cloud Innovation Center, he established a “permit to fail” learning environment. Teams had avoided risks because they feared blame. Matt organized non-punitive post-mortems, emphasized lessons rather than finger-pointing, and supported low-stakes experiments with structured hypotheses and controlled iterations. Teams applied those lessons in subsequent sprints to prevent recurring failure patterns.

He also brought engineers, product managers, and UX architects together in balanced teams with equal participation and shared accountability. Instead of handing work between separate functions, they used pair programming, collaborative coding, retrospectives, and real-time feedback. Matt connected team goals to client and business outcomes and gave teams room to change their own workflows.

At the Cloud Innovation Center, teams accelerated delivery **4x** after embracing lean product and modern engineering practices. His balanced-team work also achieved **zero-defect production code** through iterative development and real-time feedback loops.

🐾 Here’s what Matt has built, shipped, and left in place.

Matt’s work spans Execution & Delivery, Org & Working-Model Transformation, and Talent & Enablement: delivering enterprise platforms, building the organization that delivers them, and teaching teams the practices to continue after an engagement ends.

At **Accenture**, clients wanted to move beyond waterfall delivery and siloed teams, but new hires often lacked hands-on cloud-native experience. Engineers and clients also questioned pair programming and test-driven development: why pay for **2** engineers at **1** keyboard, and why write tests before production code?

Matt built the Atlanta and Tampa Cloud Innovation Centers from **0** to **150+** practitioners, with full P&L accountability. He established balanced teams combining product, engineering, and design. Instead of methodology presentations alone, he brought clients into the centers to observe standups, pairing, and collaborative problem-solving. Training followed an “I do, we do, you do” model, with experienced mentors and tailored learning. The talent program recorded near-zero attrition in its first **2** years.

Delivery started with business behavior expressed as Given/When/Then acceptance criteria. Teams used red-green-refactor, rotating pairs, and automated pipelines that blocked code from merging unless tests passed. At **Norfolk Southern**, mission-critical operations tools went live with **zero production defects**.

At **Capital One**, Matt assembled an **8-person** team around a client-prioritized, testable backlog and thin-slice MVPs. It delivered features **3 to 4x faster** than other **Accenture** teams on the same engagement, with **zero production defects**. The client sought to retain the team.

Across the centers, teams delivered **30+ product engagements** for **15+ Fortune 500 clients**, contributing to **\$100M+ in repeat business** through delivery excellence and client relationships. Clients requested training for their own teams, and the practices continued beyond the engagements.

At **Accenture’s** Liquid Studio, traditional training programs couldn’t keep pace with rapidly evolving AWS technologies. Engineers had gaps in cloud competency, and cloud adoption was slowing. The Atlanta Innovation Hub needed a structured cloud enablement program that would prepare engineers for cloud-native transformation initiatives, not just certification exams.

Matt led AWS Launchpad from **July 2018** to **November 2019**, working in collaboration with AWS to build deep cloud competencies across **Accenture**. He designed structured learning paths and certification programs around AWS core services, including Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, Kubernetes, and ECS/Fargate, alongside cloud-native application development.

Rather than relying on theory alone, he delivered interactive workshops and hands-on labs that immersed engineers in real-world AWS environments. Practical application was built into the training, so engineers could work with the technologies they were learning.

He also established cloud expert mentorship teams to embed AWS best practices and retain institutional knowledge. Group coaching sessions and knowledge-sharing workshops gave participants ongoing support alongside the structured learning paths. The program combined certification preparation, practical work, and access to experienced cloud practitioners rather than treating training as a standalone course.

Over **200 professionals earned AWS certifications**, including Solutions Architect and DevOps Engineer certifications. The program accelerated cloud adoption and the launch of cloud-native initiatives, while establishing mentorship and knowledge-sharing practices for continued learning across teams.
